column1: # word-win-font-map.tsv: for every font NAME the 756 + LibreOffice documents request, the face(s) Word for Windows actually drew.
# Windows 01QbbApP, 2026-11-01, Word 16.0.20430, Windows 11 (this box's fonts + the Chinese supplemental font packs). Built by test/corpus/docx/fmap.py
# from the word-win reference PDFs (embedded font names, subset prefix stripped) of 1349 documents.
# Method: each character of each run is attributed to the name its run resolves to (run rFonts, character/paragraph style chain,
# docDefaults, theme fonts; ascii/hAnsi for non-CJK, eastAsia for CJK). A character attributed to ONE name credits (name, face) for
# every face that drew it. 'docs' = documents where (name, face) occurred; 'chars' = distinct characters credited per document, summed;
# 'share' = chars of this face / all chars credited to the name. Rows under 3% share are omitted; a face under 15% is usually the
# fallback for characters the primary face lacks (X+Y), a bold/italic cut, or a mis-attributed neutral character (digits, punctuation).
# 'installed' = the name is a font family on this box ('yes'), a registry font ('yes(reg)'), a FontSubstitutes alias ('subst->X'), or
# 'yes(cloud)' (in Word's cloud font cache: Aptos, DengXian, FangSong, KaiTi, MS Mincho, MingLiU, PMingLiU, Noto Sans, Open Sans, ...), or
# 'NO' (not installed: Word substituted — see word-win-missing-faces-map.txt for the substitution per font-table entry).
# '___WRD_EMBED_SUB_n' = a font embedded in the document itself (obfuscated .odttf), not an installed face.
